DIRECTION OWNER: direction.absorption_is_reversal, narrowly scoped to the completed Sep-25 EIA-born absorption state and confirmed by paired price response. Sep-25 on NGX25 opened 3.145 and closed 3.219 for +$740, with a +$1,160 high excursion and only -$140 low excursion. Against that positive price path, aggregate signed flow was -6,427 lots: phase 2 delivered +$730 while signed flow was -5,697 and phase 3 still delivered +$40 against -672, with absorb_session=true and ph_absorb=true in both phases. This is not a raw-flow call; it is the opposite: heavy selling failed to push price down and was absorbed while price repriced higher. The current brain's direction.absorption_is_reversal says absorbed sell -> UP. Its full-population audit is weak at 11/22 next-day calls, so I do not grant the broad form authority. But the same audit identifies the EIA-print subset as the only slice that clears (4/6), and Sep-25 is exactly an EIA print session. That narrower EIA-born form is the sign owner here. E's specialist guard independently requires price response and turn evidence before Friday/roll flow can own sign, which is satisfied by the paired +$740 price / -6.4k flow disagreement; gross program or roll flow itself is not used. The prior session did not register a turn (turn_kind=none), and its close retained roughly two-thirds of the full low-to-high range rather than fully round-tripping the impulse. That supports holding rather than an immediate fade, but the +$420 give-back from the +$1,160 high keeps confidence low. structure.covering_absorption_directional_tell is stood down because its crowded-short gate fails badly (managed-money 1y percentile 57.55, not <~12), so I am not calling a classic crowded-short covering squeeze. boundary.prior_close_flow_direction_disagreement is also not allowed to own sign; it is subordinate to the stronger EIA-specific absorption mechanism. magnitude.terminal_impact_coefficient_carry does not justify a tiny <=$200 net: the final phase has |-672| lots and +$40 price change, an impact coefficient about 0.060, just above the play's <=0.05 numb threshold, and its broad audit materially weakens the original effect size. Friday is futures-expiry and bidweek day 3, so the distribution is widened for settlement mechanics, but current NGX25 contract-structure/options/squeeze data is unavailable under the historical mask; expiry proximity is therefore magnitude/tail context, not a second sign owner. I center the day at +$380, below the prior EIA session's +$740 impulse, with a late expiry lift and modest settlement give-back. Slow grid/storage/demand state is not used to create the UP sign.
